listings.name: Amsterdam Boats B.V.
listings.content: Personal rental of a wide variety of boats. You can rent a gondola, hand made by a girl from Amsterdam. She traveled to Venice to learn the craft, then built her own Gondola which she brought back to Amsterdam.

listings.name: Amsterdam Jewel Cruises
listings.content: An evening dinner cruise. It is the only classic boat offering a private table for a romantic candlelight dinner. À la carte dining, but not cheap! The cruise starts at 19:30 and lasts just under three hours.

listings.name: Boaty Rent a Boat
listings.content: Boaty Rent a Boat rents small boats (max. 6 people) to make your own private boat tour on the Amsterdam canals. These rental boats are electrically driven which means they are silent and free of exhaust fumes.

listings.name: Boats4rent Boat Rental
listings.content: Boats4rent is a boat rental where you can rent a boat without a skipper. With a three or four hour rental you can make a private trip on the Amsterdam canals and the Amstel river.

listings.name: Boatboys Private Boat Tours
listings.content: Operates every day for private luxury boat tours on a historic classic boat. 1hr starting from 250.

listings.name: Canal Company
listings.content: The Canal Hopper runs three fixed routes, stopping near major attractions (Rijksmuseum, Anne Frank's House, etc.). You can get on or off as often as you like, but it is relatively expensive with 20 per 24 hours. The first boats start between 09:15 and 10:45, depending on which stop you get on. The last boats start dropping off at around 19:00. It also has four locations for renting your own boat; two-seater canal bikes cost 8 per person per hour.

listings.name: Lovers Company
listings.content: Starts opposite the Rijksmuseum, but you cannot get on or off. The cruise takes about 1 hr 30 min.

listings.name: Sloepdelen
listings.content: Self operated electric rental boats. A boating license is not required and the open boats can seat up to twelve passengers.
listings.price: 60 p/h (with a minimum of 2 hours) plus 150 deposit)

listings.name: Amsterdam Boat Experience
listings.content: Amsterdam Boat Experience was founded in 2015 and has been steadily expanding its fleet and now offers exclusive private charters while also operating a fixed route from the Anne Frank house. Tickets for the 1 hour cruise on the luxurious electric open boats with live narrating are 15. while you relax the hostess serves drinks on the boat.

listings.name: Adam's Boats
listings.content: Rent a boat without the need for a licence. The Amstel river can be reached within 2 minutes from the hire place.

listings.name: Starboard Boats
listings.content: This eco friendly boat company organises luxurious private boat rentals. Starting locations on requests. From 195 per hour.

listings.name: Chinese New Year
listings.content: Celebrated with festivities in Chinatown.

listings.name: King's Day
listings.content: Formerly Queen's Day, this national holiday, nominally in celebration of the King's birthday, is difficult to describe to anyone who's never been there. The city turns into one giant mass of orange-dressed people with flea markets, bands playing, and many on-street parties, ranging from small cafes placing a few kegs of beer outside to huge open-air stages hosting world-famous DJs. The Vondelpark is the place where children sell toys and perform. An experience you'll never forget. Normally held on April 27, but if that is a Sunday, it is celebrated one day earlier.

listings.name: KunstRAI
listings.content: A modern art fair in the RAI exhibition and conference centre. If you want to know what the latest developments are in Dutch galleries, this is where to find them all in one place.

listings.name: Holland Festival
listings.content: A performing arts festival that brings together events from all over the world in the fields of music, opera, theater and dance.

listings.name: Taste of Amsterdam
listings.content: A culinary festival where you can explore the food of famous Amsterdam restaurants and their chefs.

listings.name: Open Garden Days
listings.content: Normally you can see only the front of the canal houses, but during the Open Garden Days you get to go past the entrance and see the green world behind them, often bigger than you would have expected. You can buy one ticket that gives you entry to all participating gardens, and there is a special canal boat to take you from one location to another.

listings.name: Amsterdam Roots Festival
listings.content: A free open-air festival with music from non-Western countries accompanied by paid film and theater performances in the surrounding theaters.

listings.name: Julidans
listings.content: International contemporary dance festival, always showing the latest developments in modern dance.

listings.name: Vondelpark Openluchttheater
listings.content: This free festival offers many different performances every day. Go to the open air theater just by the fountain and let the entertainment do the work. From cabaret to drama to concerts to dance, there is something for everyone here and for all ages.

listings.name: Amsterdam International Fashion Week
listings.content: Twice a year, this event presents young and upcoming fashion in Europe with a focus on Dutch design.

listings.name: VriendenLoterij SummerConcerts
listings.content: Affordable classical music concerts taking place at the prestigious Concertgebouw.

listings.name: De Parade
listings.content: Circus turns vintage, on an old-fashioned fairground with many different tents, the performers are each trying to attract their public, featuring spectacles of dance, theater, magic, art, animation and music.

listings.name: Pride Amsterdam
listings.content: Amsterdam's LGBTQIA+ pride around the first weekend in August. One of the biggest festivals in Amsterdam with parties, performances, workshops and a boat parade on the Prinsengracht on Saturday afternoon (Canal parade) which is always well worth seeing by gays and straights alike.

listings.name: Prinsengrachtconcert and Grachtenfestival
listings.content: Third weekend of August each year. A free open-air classical music concert is held every year on a stage in the middle of the Prinsengracht. If you have a little boat, join the crowds and make sure to bring a bottle of rose wine or prosecco for full enjoyment. It takes place during the Grachtenfestival, a 10 days classical music festival with about 150 concerts throughout the city, but is organized independently from it.

listings.name: Sail Amsterdam
listings.content: Tall-ships from all over the world come to visit the Amsterdam harbour every five years, the next one is planned in 2030.

listings.name: National Restaurant Week
listings.content: Two times a year, participating restaurants offer a full 3 course dinner for a mere 29.95 (excluding drinks), allowing you to try a different restaurant for a change or a chance to have an affordable meal at one of the famous five-star restaurants.

listings.name: Amsterdam Dance Event
listings.content: Usually held during the second last weekend in October, this electronic music annual festival gathers cream of the crop faces from the house and techno scenes. Buy your tickets in advance to avoid paying more at the door and having to queue for hours. Besides partying for four nights in a row, the conference offers workshops, seminars, presentations etc.

listings.name: Museumnacht
listings.content: Long before the film came out, this "night at the museum" attracts new crowds at the traditional Amsterdam museums with special performances at unusual locations. Do as the locals do and hire a bike to go from one place to the other.

listings.name: PAN Amsterdam
listings.content: The biggest national art and antiques fair in the Netherlands.

listings.name: International Documentary Film Festival (IDFA)
listings.content: The largest festival in the world for documentary films with screenings of about 200 documentary films and videos.

listings.name: Imagine Film Festival
listings.content: A two weeks celebration of drive-in, exploitation and cult films, generally of the lower budget variety. Takes up all the screening rooms of the EYE Film Institute in Noord.

listings.name: Museumplein
listings.content: Amsterdam celebrates the holy day of Sint Nicholaas on 5 December as Christmas in the Dam Square also known as "Christmas Square". However, on Christmas Day, i.e. 25 December, the people of Amsterdam are also getting used to celebrating Christmas alongside English speakers.

listings.name: Amsterdam Light Festival
listings.content: Outdoor light installations/artworks exposition in the canals of Binnenstad. Each year the festival has a different theme.

listings.name: Magere Brug
listings.content: The Magere Brug, literally "Skinny Bridge", is a bridge that spans the Amstel River and connects the Kerkstraat with the Nieuwe Kerkstraat. It's an iconic bridge that consists of nine arches and a drawbridge that is still operated by hand. The current bridge is made of white-painted wood, but it has been rebuilt several times and historically it has also been in concrete. The first bridge here was built in 1691, but the current one dates from 1934. It is one of the most photographed bridges in Amsterdam, especially at night because of the 1200 tiny lights that make it look like a picture-perfect postcard.

listings.name: Anne Frank House
listings.content: The house where the Jewish girl Anne Frank wrote her diary while hiding with her family from the Nazis. One must buy tickets online, only 20% are issued on the same day so buy them in advance. During high season tickets can be sold out a month in advance. To be safe, you should book 6 weeks in advance. Museumkaart is valid, I Amsterdam Card is not valid.

listings.name: Museum Het Grachtenhuis
listings.content: Het Grachtenhuis is the gateway to the world-famous Canal District. Het Grachtenhuis tells the fascinating story of how Amsterdam's Canal District was created by a multi-media exhibition.

listings.name: Cat Cabinet
listings.content: A cat museum. Housed in a beautiful restored palatial home in an upscale area street - very Masterpiece Theater. It was opened by the homeowner after his favourite cat died... and he still lives in the home. Lots of cat-related art, and two real felines. The exhibition is spread across the first floor of the house.
listings.image: Cat Cabinet face Amsterdam-Photo by Pejman Akbarzadeh Persian Dutch Network.jpg

listings.name: Museum Willet-Holthuysen
listings.content: It is the only fully furnished canalside patrician house in Amsterdam that is open to the public. The museum has a large collection of silverware, plates, and books from the Dutch Golden Age. It also has a substantial collection of art.

listings.name: Amsterdam Pipe Museum
listings.content: Unique collection of smoking pipes in an authentic canal house from 1670. In the historic ambience of the collector's house, his collection of pipes covering 2,500 years is displayed. Visitors get a personal tour by enthusiast volunteers of the foundation that also runs the speciality shop in the basement: a huge selection of nearly 3,000 modern briar pipes are for sale, next to collectables and books on pipes and tobacco.

listings.name: Museum Van Loon
listings.content: 17th century house with interior restored with furnishings to how it looked in the 18th century. Also interesting to see a garden you would not normally see from the streets.

listings.name: Foam
listings.content: Museum about photography. Group tours can be arranged via phone at +31 20 5516 505.

listings.name: Westerkerk
listings.content: Built in 1620-1631, located on Westermarkt near the Anne Frank House. You can climb the tower (with a guide only) every half hour, M-Sa €6. The tower is also open in the winter by group appointment (maximum 10 people) for €70/hr. In good weather you can see all of Amsterdam, and as far as the coast. Free organ concert held every Friday at 13:00.

listings.name: Homomonument
listings.content: The Homomonument is a memorial to gays and lesbians murdered in World War II, a call for vigilance against homophobia, and an inspiration for gays and lesbians the world over. It consists of three equilateral triangles made of pink granite that are connected by an inlaid band of pink bricks. These three triangles represent the past, present and future.

listings.name: Rembrandtplein
listings.content: This public square features a larger-than-life statue of Rembrandt on a pedestal.

listings.name: De Poezenboot
listings.content: You really like cats? The poezenboot (cat boat) is a refuge for cats awaiting adoption.

listings.name: Ignatiushuis
listings.content: A Jesuit society that organizes classes and activities. Membership is required, but every Tuesday (Sep-Jul) a free concert is given at 12:30-13:00. Everyone can attend.

listings.name: Pathé Tuschinski
listings.content: Since its opening in 1921, Tuschinski has been the country's most breathtaking film theatre. It's worth a visit if only for its interior, a spectacular mix of Art Nouveau, Amsterdam School and Art Deco styles. If possible, get a tour of the building, taking in the sumptuous private rooms upstairs. If you're going to watch a film, pick the one that's in the big auditorium. With the exception of some animated films, all English films are subtitled and not dubbed, so you should be able to enjoy the standard Hollywood fare the way it's meant to be seen.

listings.name: Stadsarchief Amsterdam
listings.content: This institute maintains the archives of the municipality and other organizations that are closely related to Amsterdam. The archives are open to everyone. Most interesting for travelers are the exhibitions and events, see the website.

listings.name: Amsterdam Booze Cruise
listings.content: A boat trip through the canals of Amsterdam is always a good idea. Discover Amsterdam from the water while enjoying a drink.

listings.name: Pancakes! Amsterdam
listings.content: Amazing variety of both sweet and savory pancakes. The quaint atmosphere and the street side tables are great for watching people. The only downfall is that street-side tables attract too many tourists asking for directions.

listings.name: The Pancake Bakery
listings.content: Large selection of sweet or savory pancakes.

listings.name: Frens Haringhandel
listings.content: A stall offering simple Dutch seafood fare like Kibbling (fried fish) and Haring (raw herring).

listings.name: De Blauwe Hollander
listings.content: Dutch restaurant with an extensive menu of hearty home-cooked dishes like herrings, pea soup and hutspot. Unlike most restaurants in this area, this one gets local diners too, and if it gets crowded enough you may have to share tables. Pancakes are served only until 17:00.

listings.name: Damsteeg
listings.content: They specialise in fish dishes, but they also have a wide variety of meat and vegetarian meals to choose from. With bar.

listings.name: Letting
listings.content: Indian-owned breakfast, brunch and lunch spot. Letting offers a range of soups, sandwiches and scones, and it's on a street which is packed with an ever-changing line-up of fun boutiques.

listings.name: Holtkamp
listings.content: Best pastry cafe in Amsterdam. Much better than the Zeitan, which many recommend. Do try the "holdkampf" with fillings! The Sachertorte is famous as a favorite of the former Queen Beatrix.

listings.name: Alberto's Steakhouse
listings.content: Uruguayan Steakhouse with well-grilled steaks

listings.name: Akbar
listings.content: Indian restaurant, Muslim (halal) / Hindu (no beef). Good quality dishes from different regions of India.

listings.name: La Margarita
listings.content: This Caribbean restaurant offers a huge range of plates, including three different vegetarian options. Every dish comes with ample sides of white rice, black beans, plantains, and vegetables. In addition to having great food, the restaurant is decked out with a range of fantastic and magic-realist art. If you like your food hot, then be sure to ask for the special homemade hot sauce. Reservations accepted.

listings.name: 't Arendsnest
listings.content: Excellent biercafe serving only Dutch beers and liqueurs, including jenever. Around 30 beers on tap, 17 or so which change regularly, and over 100 bottled. Very friendly bartenders who know beer well and give great recommendations. Try the €8 sampler, which gives you 12cl (1.2ml) samples of 3 beers with a glass of water and some crackers.

listings.name: Dan Murphy's
listings.content: One of the many Irish pubs in the city. People from all over the world meet here and watch football, rugby and typical Irish sports like hurling and Gaelic football while drinking a pint of Guinness.

listings.name: Feijoa
listings.content: Cocktail bar with a lovely atmosphere, pleasant music and friendly staff, including one of the Netherlands leading cocktail barmen. Will make any cocktail you ask for.

listings.name: Hard Rock Cafe
listings.content: This is close to, or right next to the Holland Casino also close to the Leidseplein. Great service, great food, and plenty of drinks.

listings.name: Mulligans Irish Music Bar
listings.content: The oldest Irish bar in Amsterdam, Mulligans has live music most nights. This is where the traditional music crowd gathers.

listings.name: l'Opera
listings.content: A friendly spot for coffee, a beer, or something stronger. You may at first only notice the outside seating and the enclosed terrace, but there is also an elegant, (usually) quieter indoor area. Food, too, but you don't see many eaters.

listings.name: Whisky Cafe L&B
listings.content: If you like whisky, this small, laid-back and friendly cafe is the ideal place to visit. Many unusual whiskies from independent bottlers and closed distilleries are available. The menu stretches along one wall and is about 2 meters in height, the cafe having had 1001 whiskies available since it opened. Just be warned the stairs to the toilets are pretty steep!

listings.name: Chicago Social Club
listings.content: Amsterdam's nightlife king Casper Reinders joined with the founders of Bitterzoet and the owners of Boom Chicago to bring quality clubbing to the Leidspelein.

listings.name: Escape
listings.content: A large, fairly uninspiring nightclub that mostly plays mainstream house music. The first hall is large and attracts the more or less wannabe hip people of the city, although the crowd is diverse. The second hall upstairs has a completely different audience, mostly hip-hop and R&B enthusiasts. At some events, Escape is split in two, which means you can use the backside entry at Amstel for a different party.

listings.name: Jimmy Woo
listings.content: The most glamorous club in Amsterdam offers a selection of house and R&B, with a spectacularly lit dance floor downstairs. It is relatively small and there is table service, so it feels a bit like a VIP room. Entry policy is strict so dress sharp to get in. And boys, don't come alone.

listings.name: Melkweg
listings.content: A former milk factory, now it's one of the best live venues in Amsterdam. Its interior is not as good as Paradiso, but it feels more like a nightclub as the music is dance/trance-oriented. Popular among university students and younger tourists, it's a great place to go out till the sun gets up. Rates can vary widely, and go very steep during special events.

listings.name: Paradiso
listings.content: Sometimes referred to as a nightclub, it feels more like a nightly music venue and is the safest bet in town. Its interior is phenomenal as it is housed in a former church, but the main room has relatively bad acoustics. It gets a mixed crowd as there are plenty of rooms with different bands performing and it isn't too crazy expensive. Its music straddles the line between pop and alternative. Much of the performances are rock, but it can really be anything: don't be surprised to be dancing the Russian troika with thousands of people on a Wednesday night. It gets fairly packed, as is obvious by the huge line on the weekends, especially after 01:00.

listings.name: Studio 80
listings.content: This is a somewhat more underground, intimate club that's easy to miss because of its flashy neighbours. It prides itself on trying to stay at the forefront of electronic music in the city.

listings.name: Sugar Factory
listings.content: Bit of a remarkable place that integrates art, music, culture, theatre and nightclub into one. It has a relaxed atmosphere with an eccentric, artistic audience.

listings.name: The Cave Rockclub
listings.content: Cozy metal bar with friendly bar staff and interesting regulars, with live performances by touring metal bands on weekends.

listings.name: Waterhole
listings.content: Light rock/funk jam sessions in a dingy but atmospheric bar with pooltables. Live bands play every night of the week.

listings.name: Betty Too
listings.content: Absolute gem, cozy and friendly place with moderate prizes and interesting, international crowd.

listings.name: Bulldog
listings.content: This is the original shop that used to be a police department. Now it turned into a chain of touristy coffeeshops, bars, hotels and even an energy drink.

listings.name: Global Chillage
listings.content: Good produce and nice tunes but uncomfortable seating.

listings.name: Grey Area
listings.content: Tiny, but famous for their outstanding weed, especially "American" strains.

listings.name: The Otherside
listings.content: Gay coffeeshop.

listings.name: Hans Brinker Hostel
listings.content: Very light atmosphere and doesn't take itself seriously. Bar and downstairs club.

listings.name: Mozart Hotel
listings.content: 47 en-suite rooms.

listings.name: Hotel Asterisk
listings.content: Smallish, but clean and quiet rooms in two buildings across a residential street. Generous check-in/checkout, good breakfast (included). Close to tram stop, walk to Rijks/van Gogh museums.
listings.price: €70, knock off a couple of euros by booking directly on their site

listings.name: Blue Moon Bed & Breakfast
listings.content: Bed & Breakfast opposite the Rijksmuseum.

listings.name: Cocomama
listings.content: Amsterdam's first boutique hostel. Free wifi, garden, fully equipped kitchen for guest use, livingroom. Very social atmosphere. All rooms en suite.

listings.name: Hotel La Boheme
listings.content: Two star hotel with very friendly staff. Clean rooms and free wi fi.

listings.name: Hotel Nicolaas Witsen
listings.content: 3-star hotel in the city center of Amsterdam nearby Heineken factory.

listings.name: Clayton Hotel Amsterdam American
listings.content: Listed as an Art Nouveau monument, the hotel is right in the heart of Leidseplein Square. Both Café Americain and Bar Americain are in the hotel, famous for celebrity and VIP spotting.

listings.name: Hotel Ambassade
listings.content: Four star hotel on one of the main canals. Writers who stayed here left signed copies of their books in the hotel's library.

listings.name: Hotel Pulitzer
listings.content: 25 restored 17th and 18th-century canal houses overlooking two of the city's most picturesque canals, Prinsengracht and Keizersgracht, and made famous in Ocean's 12.

listings.name: Amstelstation murals
listings.content: In the hall of Amstel railway station, there are several murals created in 1939 by Dutch artist Peter Alma, including a large mural at each end of the hall with a train motif.

listings.name: Floating houses
listings.content: There are two clusters of floating houses over a body of water. These small, modern houses are linked by a grid of walkways lined with railings holding life preservers and bicycles.

listings.name: Wereldmuseum Amsterdam
listings.content: Ethnographic and cultural museum about Africa, Asia and South America. Includes an excellent cafe which sells food from around the world. Tickets are discounted if reserved online.

listings.name: Oosterpark
listings.content: Close to Plantage, this park holds several multicultural festivals throughout the year.

listings.name: Diemerpark
listings.content: This is a large park, a little like a dune park.

listings.name: Flevopark
listings.content: The Flevopark is in the Indische Buurt, at the eastern end of the Insulindeweg, next to the Jewish cemetery, the Flevoparkbad swimming pool, and the Nieuwe Diep inlet. There are two cafés open in spring/summer/autumn time and one festival each year.

listings.name: Frankendael
listings.content: Frankendael is a house built in 1733 in Watergraafsmeer. The house is surrounded by a pleasant park. Take tram 9, get off at the stop "Hugo de Vrieslaan".

listings.name: Bimhuis
listings.content: World-class jazz and improvised music venue, five minutes by foot from Centraal Station.

listings.name: Muziekgebouw aan't IJ
listings.content: Modern music concerts and classical music with a twist. A free concert is given every second Tuesday of the month at 12:30.

listings.name: Boerenjongens Eetwinkel
listings.content: A deli shop annex lunch room with products from the region.

listings.name: IJsburg
listings.content: Ice cream shop.

listings.name: Biertuin
listings.content: Oktoberfest-style biergarten, so expect long tables and a wide variety of bottled beers available. It has a nice atmosphere during warm summer evenings. Try the Hamburger Deluxe or chicken menus. And come early, as it is often crowded. Reservations cannot be made, but you can wait outside with a beer until seating is available.

listings.name: Bloem op IJburg
listings.content: Italian restaurant.

listings.name: Silk Road Restaurant
listings.content: Eastern and Western fusion meals with both à la carte and (on highly occupied days o­nly) a live cooking theme buffet. The restaurant has a view of the river IJ. Open 7 days per week for lunch and dinner.

listings.name: Espressofabriek
listings.content: Coffee bar.

listings.name: N.A.P.
listings.content: A harbour-side cafe and restaurant with a view of the marina. You can just stop by for a cup of coffee, have breakfast, lunch or dinner. Stylish interior.

listings.name: Delirium Café Amsterdam
listings.content: With over 500 bottled beers and 20 craft beers on draft, the biggest craft beer bar in Amsterdam.

listings.name: Panama
listings.content: This nightclub is relatively close to the city centre. It has its fair share of nice nights and the view on the water is excellent.

listings.name: Canvas
listings.content: A restaurant-bar-club, this urban and edgy den in a former newspaper office is a great place to go out at night. With nice views of the city and a varied music repertoire (alternative, jazz, funk), it's one of the hidden secrets too often overlooked by foreign visitors. Try one of the cocktails.

listings.name: Camping Zeeburg
listings.content: This campground is near the city. It has camping cabins, wagonettes, tent sites and RV sites. A good store, free wifi and restaurant/bar round out the amenities. A good, clean and cheap place to stay if you do not mind walking to the bathroom and paying €.80 for a hot shower.

listings.name: Stayokay Zeeburg
listings.content: This 480-bed hostel is located to the east of the city centre in a typical Amsterdam neighbourhood. Amsterdam's historic centre is less than 15 minutes away by bike or tram. The hostel is in the same building as Studio K, a budget diner and movie theatre. Children under 12 must stay in private rooms and everyone under 18 must be accompanied by an adult.

listings.name: Generator Hostel Amsterdam
listings.content: This former university building can host up to 564 guests in twin and quadruple rooms. It has spacious social areas with creative design touches all over the building. The old lecture rooms and hall have been turned into bars and a relaxation room. This place is excellent value for groups and budget travellers, with quadruple rooms for €60 or single (bunk) beds in shared rooms for €15. Bathrooms are en-suite. If you're under 18 and travelling without an adult, you'll need written consent from your parents and you'll need to book a private room.

listings.name: Bastion Hotel Amsterdam Amstel
listings.content: 3 star-hotel with 192 rooms. Due to its central location, the Amsterdam RAI, Amsterdam ArenA and Ziggo Dome are very well accessible from Bastion Hotel Amsterdam Amstel. Public transport is located within a 10-minute walk.

listings.name: Mövenpick Hotel
listings.content: The hotel is in the Eastern Docklands, the renewed area of the city centre.

listings.name: Brouwersgracht
listings.content: This canal is sometimes cited as the "most beautiful street of Amsterdam". The name, "Brewer's Canal", refers to the many beer breweries along the canal in the 16th and 17th centuries. Nowadays, there's just one distillery left, De Ooievaar, that has been located here since 1782 and specializes in Dutch jenever and liquors. The warehouses here used to store goods such as coffee, spices and leather, but now serve a residential purpose. Traditional warehouses with the row of spout gables can be found at Brouwersgracht 196–188, and at 204, 206, 208 and 210. Also check out the wide-open red shutters at Groene Valk (192) and Grouwe Valk (194). Geloof, Brouwersgracht 218, shows the typical "neck" gable designed by Philips Vingboons.

listings.name: Pianola Museum
listings.content: A museum about Pianolas from the early 1900s. About a dozen are displayed at any one time, and every month a piano concert is held.

listings.name: Boom Chicago
listings.content: The Amsterdam comedy institution since 1993. English language sketch and improv comedy show with extensive use of video, music and the internet. The troupe is sharp and skewers current events, trends and life and local events in Amsterdam. Perhaps the best comedy show in any city. Good food is served before the show and drink service continues all night.

listings.name: Ken Tui Massage
listings.content: Offers a quality massage.

listings.name: Burgermeester
listings.content: Yes, they serve burgers here. But don't expect a McDonalds wannabe. They are quality meat, fish or vegetarian burgers. The place is so popular that they opened 2 more branches in the city. Great if you want to have a quick and inexpensive bite. Order the 'mini trio' so you can taste three different small sized burgers.

listings.name: Kinnaree
listings.content: Amazing Thai food. Good atmosphere, good service despite being quite busy, but the food is why you would come here. Highly recommended.

listings.name: Long Pura
listings.content: Indonesian food, try the rice table.

listings.name: Proeverij 274
listings.content: Small, cosy restaurant at one of the main canals. Business but also romantic dinner. Small menu, new Dutch cuisine with classic French influences. The menu features mainly organic regional produce. Personal service, nice wine advice and fresh seasonal food in a relaxed environment.

listings.name: Maloe Melo
listings.content: Small blues bar which is separated in two parts: a free part in the front, €5 entrance fee in the back where blues or rock 'n' roll bands play live every night of the week.

listings.name: 't Smalle
listings.content: Some say this place has the most beautiful terrace in Amsterdam. It's not big but you sit right beside the canal. And if it's too cold to sit outside check out the beautifully restored interior in this laid-back place.

listings.name: Cafe P 96
listings.content: Great character at this pub, lovely outdoor terrace on a houseboat makes for a nice evening or afternoon. Good selection of Dutch and Belgian beers.

listings.name: Soundgarden
listings.content: Top metal/grungy/punky pub, most relaxed drinking atmosphere in town. Really nice, secluded terrace for drinking beer in the sun. can smoke, but not buy, puff.

listings.name: Bar Brandstof
listings.content: Relatively new bar with a big and often busy terrace. Gets absolutely crowded on Friday after work hours

listings.name: Bar Struik
listings.content: Hangout for the urban 20 and 30-somethings. Every day except Friday they serve 1 dish for 7.50. Gets really crowded in the weekends.

listings.name: Cafe Chaos
listings.content: Typical Amsterdam brown bar. Throw your peanuts shells on the floor while looking at the furniture.

listings.name: Maloe Melo
listings.content: Live 1950s rockabilly bar. Drinks are cheap and the crowd are mostly Dutch rockers, but the music is good.

listings.name: Barney's
listings.content: Coffeeshop.

listings.name: Coffeeshop Ibiza
listings.content: Big coffee shop.

listings.name: Shelter Jordan Hostel
listings.content: An alcohol and drug-free Christian youth hostel. Single-sex dormitories (including breakfast, bed linen).

listings.name: Hotel de Paris
listings.content: The hotel has 48 rooms, and is located near the Waterlooplein flee market. Average to good online ratings.

listings.name: Hotel De Looier Amsterdam
listings.content: The hotel is a - star hotel located near many of the main Museums of Amsterdam. Hotel De Looier Amsterdam was built as a diamond factory in 1886.

listings.name: Marnix Hotel
listings.content: 2-star hotel with dorm beds.

listings.name: D'Admiraal (1792)
listings.content: Windmill on the bank of the Noordhollands Kanaal in the north, ferry from Central Station.

listings.name: STRAAT Museum
listings.content: Museum depicting street art in a large indoor exhibition.

listings.name: EYE Film Institute Netherlands
listings.content: EYE is an institute dedicated to the preservation of film for future generations. It is the successor of the Filmmuseum. It has four film theatres with alternative screenings such as art films. In April the Imagine Film Festival is held here with screenings dedicated to exploitation, cult and lower-budget films. Well worth it if you're a fan of the genre.

listings.name: Café Modern B.V.
listings.content: A restaurant and cafe in a hall which used to be a bank.

listings.name: Café-restaurant Stork
listings.content: A fish and seafood restaurant in an old factory on the banks of the river.

listings.name: Hangar Amsterdam
listings.content: A redesigned aircraft hangar, turned restaurant.

listings.name: Mount Everest Tandoori
listings.content: An Indian and Nepalese restaurant. Vegetarian friendly.

listings.name: Pllek
listings.content: A bar and restaurant in an old industrial area, by the river.

listings.name: Bastion Hotel Amsterdam Noord
listings.content: 3-star hotel with 86 rooms.

listings.name: Amsterdam Centraal railway station
listings.content: This beautiful building is an attraction in itself, so if you did not arrive in Amsterdam by train, it is well worth making a special trip to look at the station's facade. The station was built between 1881 and 1889 on three artificial islands. It was designed by Pierre Cuypers who also designed the Rijksmuseum in a similar neo-late-Gothic/Renaissance style. At the time, the project was highly controversial as the new station would effectively cut off the city from the IJ waterfront. Politicians in The Hague pushed it through anyway, and now it is widely regarded as the most beautiful station in the country.
listings.image: Estación Central, Ámsterdam, Países Bajos, 2016-05-30, DD 01-03 HDR.jpg

listings.name: Beurs van Berlage
listings.content: Take a guided tour and check out the view from the top of the old stock exchange tower. It was built in 1903 (by Hendrik Petrus Berlage) and is considered the beginning of modern Dutch architecture. Costs €3.50, located on Beursplein near Dam Square.

listings.name: Royal Palace
listings.content: The Royal Palace is one of the three official palaces of the Netherlands. It is at the disposal of King Willem-Alexander by the Act of Parliament. It was built in 1651 as the city hall of Amsterdam, in a period known as the Dutch Golden Age. Many school children learn that because of the swampy soil, it was built on no less than 13,569 wooden poles. In 1795, the French Empire of Napoleon Bonaparte invaded the Netherlands, and his brother Louis Napoleon became the first King of Holland in 1806. He acquired the city hall in that year and turned it into a royal palace. It was restored to the original owners when Prince William VI returned to the Netherlands in 1812, but when he was crowned as King William I, he decided that Amsterdam should be the official capital and acquired the city hall once again as a royal palace. This is still a delicate subject among the locals, some of whom would like to see the palace returned to Amsterdam. It was completely renovated in 2009. It is mainly used for diplomatic receptions and to welcome visiting heads of state, not as a royal residence.

listings.name: Nationaal Monument
listings.content: A large spire that functions as a memorial for the victims of World War II. It was designed by architect J.J.P. Oud and revealed on 4 May 1956. Every 4 May, at the Remembrance of the Dead, a ceremony is held here to commemorate all civilians and members of the Dutch armed forces that died in World War II and later armed conflicts.
listings.image: Amsterdam nationaal monument op de dam februari 2003.jpg

listings.name: Begijnhof
listings.content: The Begijnhof is a late medieval enclosed courtyard with the houses of beguines (Roman Catholic women living in a semi-religious community). It is a very picturesque group of historic buildings, mostly private dwellings. House number 34 is the oldest home in Amsterdam. The courtyard also has a Reformed Church and a hidden Catholic chapel. Surprisingly, it feels like a serene oasis as it is surrounded by the chaotic Kalverstraat and Spui. Entry to the courtyard and surrounding gardens is free, but be careful not to disturb the local community still living here.

listings.name: Esnoga
listings.content: The most prominent synagogue of the city centre, the Esnoga dates back from 1675 and is built in an austere Classicist style. In 1492, Spain expelled its Jewish population as part of the Inquisition, and many fled to Portugal. One hundred years later, their descendants migrated to Amsterdam for its religious freedom. This happened at a time when the Dutch provinces were fighting for independence against Spain. As to avoid being related to the enemy, these Jewish refugees originally from Spain began to refer to themselves as "Portuguese Jews". In the early 16th century, the three Jewish communities that existed at the time merged to form the Portuguese Jewish Community of Amsterdam, which still exists today. They were joined by Ashkenazi Jews that arrived from Central and Eastern Europe in the 17th century, together forming the largest Jewish community in Amsterdam and the Netherlands. Shabbat services are held regularly.

listings.name: Nieuwe Kerk
listings.content: Used for royal coronations, including the crowning of King Willem-Alexander in 2013, and royal weddings, including his wedding to princess Máxima in 2002. The church is no longer used for services but is now a popular exhibition space. Admissions are limited: by tickets online to reserve a space.
listings.price: By credit/debit card only: adult €19.50, student/youth €9.50, child under 12 free, free with Museumkaart

listings.name: Oude Kerk
listings.content: The oldest of the five main churches in the historic centre, and probably the oldest building in Amsterdam. It is right in the heart of the Red Light District. You can climb the tower from April to September on Saturday and Sunday, every half-hour. Also open in the winter by group appointment (maximum 10 people) cost €70 per hour. E-mail for more information.

listings.name: Zuiderkerk
listings.content: Built in 1603-1611. Located on Zuiderkerkhof ("Southern Graveyard"). Now an information centre on housing and planning. You can visit the tower from April to September Monday to Saturday (with guide only) every half-hour, cost €6. Also open in the winter by group appointment (maximum 15 people) cost €70 per hr. E-mail for more information.

listings.name: Allard Pierson Museum
listings.content: The Allard Pierson Museum is the archaeological museum of the University of Amsterdam. The ancient civilizations of Egypt, Cyprus, the Greek world, Etruria and the Roman Empire are revived in this museum. Art objects and utensils, dating from 4000 B.C. till 500 A.D. give a good impression of everyday life, mythology and religion in Antiquity.

listings.name: Amsterdam Museum
listings.content: A museum about the history of Amsterdam.

listings.name: Civic Guards Gallery
listings.content: Just inside the arched gateway to the Amsterdam Museum is a hidden passageway with fifteen enormous 17th-century paintings; entrance is free to the public during museum hours. The collection features massive and meticulously realistic portraits of wealthy citizens from the Dutch Golden Age, the same class of subjects Rembrandt depicted in the most famous of Civic Guard paintings, the "Night Watch".
listings.image: Schuttersgalerij naar het noorden - Amsterdam - 20014295 - RCE.jpg

listings.name: Jewish Historical Museum
listings.content: Jewish Historical Museum. History of the Jewish people, culture and religion.

listings.name: Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder
listings.content: One of the oldest museums in Amsterdam, this is a Catholic church stuffed into the upper stories of a house built in 1663, when Catholics were persecuted and had to disguise their churches. It's amazing to see how they fit worshippers, an organ, and an altar into such a narrow place.
listings.image: Amsterdam - Museum Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder - hidden church.JPG

listings.name: Oranje Voetbal Museum
listings.content: The legacy of Dutch football started in the 1970s, when Total Football, a revolutionary Dutch style of football, shook the world. The Netherlands is the best football nation that never won the World Cup: it lost the final three times, a national trauma. It did win the European Cup in 1988 lead by star player Marco van Basten. This museum has four floors dedicated to "Oranje", and a small cinema that shows a 20-minute film with historic football moments. Especially recommended for Germans.

listings.name: Rembrandt House
listings.content: This is where the artist Rembrandt Harmensz van Rijn and his wife, Saskia, lived between 1639 and 1658. The house is a reconstruction of the painter’s life at that time and provides interesting insight. You will be able to see 260 of his 290 etchings, find out about how they were created, see where he worked and explore the nooks and crannies of this fascinating building.

listings.name: Amsterdam Music Theatre
listings.content: Opera, dance, ballet and other performances. Holds a free lunch concert on Tuesdays.

listings.name: NEMO
listings.content: Above a tunnel overseeing the IJ, NEMO is the largest science museum in the Netherlands. It's a showcase of how scientific phenomena influence daily life. Different sections of the museum deal with technology and engineering, ICT, and bio- and behavioral sciences. This is a place to take kids and is best for those ages 11 and below—teenagers will probably get bored. And it is usually definitely full of children on weekends. During summer it has a panorama roof terrace on its roof with deckchairs with free entry.

listings.name: Gassan Diamonds
listings.content: A guided tour is given that's all about the diamond production process and the history of diamond trade in Amsterdam. Diamonds have been traded in Amsterdam for longer than 425 years, and the city used to be known as the "City of Diamonds". Tours are given in 27 languages. Of course you can also buy Gassan diamonds here, but you don't have to.

listings.name: Hash, Marihuana and Hemp Museum
listings.content: Opened for over twenty years, the Hash Museum is dedicated to debunking the lies and demonization about one of our most useful plants, the hemp plant. Although small, busy and seriously overpriced, it is a well-done museum where people go to get informed.

listings.name: Sexmuseum
listings.content: The largest and most prestigious museum for sex art and sex history in the Netherlands. It shows a lot of sex oddities. Only ages 16 and up are allowed entry.

listings.name: Madame Tussauds
listings.content: The well-known franchise of wax museums also has a branch in Amsterdam. It's a major tourist attraction so expect a steep entry fee and long queues. Unique to this branch are waxworks of famous Dutch people including Willem-Alexander, Beatrix, Tiësto, Rafael van der Vaart, Doutzen Kroes, Vincent van Gogh and Rembrandt.

listings.name: Amsterdam Dungeon
listings.content: The Amsterdam Dungeon is a horror tour through several dark chambers with live actors.

listings.name: Museum of Medieval Torture Instruments
listings.content: The latest gimmicky tourist attraction near the Centraal Station, it's a small museum about medieval torture and torture devices. In the Middle Ages, torture was a widely known punishment for almost all crimes committed, ranging from rape to murder, and above all for heresy. The type of punishment depended on the victim's crime and social status. The Museum of Medieval Torture Instruments displays over 100 devices used to torture people. Before its make-over, it used to be the Vodka Museum; the vodka shop is still open in the basement with free entry.

listings.name: Torture Museum
listings.content: You'd think one museum about torture would be enough, but no, not in Amsterdam. However, this was the first torture museum in the city centre, and is at least somewhat more authentic than the copycat. The museum depicts the history of different torturous techniques used over the centuries. The lighting is bad, the corridors are small and the price an absolute rip-off. You can walk through it in 15-30 minutes.

listings.name: Gebr. Niemeijer
listings.content: French-style bakery with pastries, croissants, breads, sandwiches all baked fresh on premises. Open for breakfast and lunch, eat-in or takeaway. Bring the kids and eat in the small playroom upstairs.

listings.name: Van der Linde
listings.content: Its officially a bakery, but they don't sell bread. They do sell Amsterdam's most famous whipped ice cream, lovely almond cookies and cakes. The texture is really creamy and soft, it melts easily and they put it in a cone with a soup spoon.

listings.name: Haring & Zo
listings.content: Serving for example fish sandwiches

listings.name: Rob Wigboldus Fishmonger
listings.content: Herring sandwiches for €3.50.

listings.name: Pasta Pasta
listings.content: Serves delicious pastas, made just as you want them. Choose a sauce, topping and pasta for a tasty, but well-priced meal.

listings.name: Julia's
listings.content: Italian cuisine, both eat-in and take-out; notable take-out item: Penne Bolognese with a tasty vegetarian sauce instead of a meat sauce.

listings.name: OCHA
listings.content: This used to be just the little "Thai snackbar around the corner", but since a raving review in the local newspaper Het Parool, big crowds are waiting in line to get seated during dinnertime. The scenery is simple and the restaurant is very small and cramped. However, the hype is all about the food, which is absolutely mouth-watering. They have the usual Thai fare, but the dish to go for is the massaman curry, their specialty.

listings.name: Thaise Snackbar Bird
listings.content: Very crowded little snack bar with Thai food. Not to be confused with the restaurant of the same owner, on the other side of the street. Try the chicken in oyster sauce.

listings.name: New King
listings.content: Slowly becoming an institution, this hugely popular Mandarin Chinese restaurant seems to have found a perfect balance between food, price and ambiance. The food is authentically Chinese, delicious, fresh and quickly served, and all of that for a bargain. Service is fast and rushed, but it doesn't feel like a snack bar. It has a stylish interior, and it's still one of those places you could bring a date to. The biggest problem is that everyone seems to know this place, so it's somewhat crowded and noisy, and you'll probably have to wait outside for a seat to become available. When you get in, order the oysters. They're a hit.

listings.name: Greetje
listings.content: Traditional Dutch, alongside French classics. Located in an historic building on a quiet side street near Central Station; it's off the beaten track so most of the diners are local. Open 6 days a week (not Mondays); a reservation is usually necessary.

listings.name: Kantjil & de Tijger
listings.content: Great spices and meat dishes, Indian/Indonesian food. Try the Nasi Goreng Rames.

listings.name: Rembrandt Corner
listings.content: Around the corner of the "Rembrandt Huis" is a very nice "Eetcafe" with fresh food, WiFi hot spots and internet workplaces. Try the dish of the day or the mussels.

listings.name: Tony's NY City Bagels
listings.content: Oversized cups of coffee, muffins and bagels. Muffins, brownies, giant cookies, cheesecake and bagels spread with various toppings are served at reasonable prices to a clientèle that is a mix of locals and tourists. American themed. There are 3 locations in the city.

listings.name: Amsterdam Jewel Cruises
listings.content: À la carte dining while cruising the canals.

listings.name: Blue
listings.content: The selling point of this cafe is its 360 degrees view over Amsterdam. Its interior is minimalist and stylish. A great place to have a Dutch cup of coffee while taking in the views. Unfortunately, it's only open at daytime as evenings are reserved for private events.

listings.name: De Jaren
listings.content: A minimal art-deco interior next to Hotel d'Europe and a great view of where all the main canals come together (climb the stairs to the upper floor - the view is better and the crowds surprisingly thinner). Food is middling and on the pricy side, but it's a nice place to sip a cup of coffee or tea and read a newspaper.

listings.name: Filter
listings.content: Small eco-friendly coffeebar situated in the lobby of hotel Ecomama. Serves great coffee, breakfast and a small selection of sweet and savoury treats. Also organic tea, juice and the best grilled-cheese sandwiches. Have a relaxed morning on the sunny terrace or enjoy art by starting Dutch artists.

listings.name: The Grasshopper
listings.content: On the edge of the Red Light District, has an upper-floor bar.

listings.name: Hannekes Boom
listings.content: One of Amsterdam's hidden secrets, Hannekes Boom is a cosy, somewhat ramshackle, bar with a waterfront along the IJ. It's a great place to just hang out and have a beer. Not for clubbers, but for those looking for a relaxing underground atmosphere and live music. It is centrally located, but off the tourist path, so it has a local feel to it. Outdoor seating is available, but you have to order your drinks inside. If you want to eat, make a reservation in advance (though the food is nothing special).

listings.name: Brouwerij de Prael
listings.content: A brewery, tasting room and beer shop all in one.
listings.price: Brewery tour 7.50 or 16.50, beer tasting with four beers €10

listings.name: Cracked Kettle
listings.content: This beer, wine, and spirits shop carries independent, unique, and rare bottles. The staff are friendly, but the space is quite confined and obtaining bottles from the very top shelves requires assistance and a dust rag.

listings.name: De Bierkoning
listings.content: Not a café, but a 'supermarket' specialized in beer. It has over a thousand beers, about half of it Dutch.

listings.name: In De Wildeman
listings.content: A very well stocked beer café, or actually beer tasting room (bierproeflokaal) in the centre of the inner city. 17 beers (usually from various countries) and a cider on draught, and about 250 different bottled beers offered. There is no music played, which makes for a very friendly and talkative atmosphere, and it has a separate non-smoking room.

listings.name: Wynand Fockink
listings.content: Wynand Fockink is a distillery that started in 1679. They offer distillery tours, but you must reserve at least a week in advance as they fill up quickly. It is also a tasting room and a liquor store. They have numerous liquors, brandies, and jenevers and encourage you to try them all. It is traditional to stoop and sip the first drink and not spill. Great liquors, and a good time in the back alleys of Amsterdam.

listings.name: Belgique
listings.content: One of the smallest bars in Amsterdam, there is seating for at most 15 people. Specialising in Belgian beers, extensive menu that includes some hard to find beers on tap. This place is smoke friendly so don't be surprised to see people rolling joints as they drink.

listings.name: Cuba
listings.content: Great bar, really nice atmosphere, close to the Red Light District with a nice terrace in the summer. Selection of cheap cocktails and long island ice tea.

listings.name: Gollem
listings.content: A special beer café, serving many beers, especially from Belgium, Germany, Czech Republic and other countries.

listings.name: Katoen
listings.content: Close to the southern part of the Canal District. Alternative music and cosy atmosphere also in the evenings.

listings.name: Molly Malones Irish Pub
listings.content: Authentic Irish pub with food. Mix of expatriates, locals and tourists, friendly staff, on a canal off the Zeedijk, close to Centraal Station and Warmoesstraat. Open every night, live music in the week-ends and large-screen television.

listings.name: Schuim
listings.content: The super comfy cafe is a great place to spend entire rainy days at a time. It heats up quite a bit at night. Pot smoking seems to be tolerated even though Schuim is definitely not a "coffeeshop".

listings.name: Speijk
listings.content: Awesome bar with lost of fun, artsy crazy locals. Various DJ play different styles. Open till late in the morning. Best place to meet laid-back and awesome Amsterdammers!!

listings.name: Irish Pub Slainte
listings.content: An Irish pub that also serves very inexpensive food like cheese sandwiches. Everything you can expect from an Irish pub nearby the Oude Kerk and nearby the Red Light District.

listings.name: Bitterzoet
listings.content: This placed used to be alternative, but changed ownership and is now more hip hop and R&B oriented. Check their agenda to see what they're doing.

listings.name: Winston Kingdom
listings.content: Music venue and nightclub in the red light district.

listings.name: 420CAFE
listings.content: Known for their moderate prices. The music played here is Classic Rock & Frank Zappa.

listings.name: Bluebird
listings.content: One of the best selections of pot in Amsterdam.

listings.name: De Dampkring
listings.content: The shop was featured in a scene in Ocean's Twelve. Very decent hashish ("Rifman" products), rather high prices. Has won the Cannabis Cup numerous times.

listings.name: Green House
listings.content: Usually pretty crowded but when warm or if you can get a seat definitely one of the nice coffeeshops near the Red Light District. Also has a bar next door.

listings.name: Hill Street Blues
listings.content: Lively atmosphere but buy cannabis elsewhere.

listings.name: Kadinsky
listings.content: It looks completely different from before, and now has three floors with a slick minimalist design.A great place to smoke your goods, and actually serves a good cup of coffee too.

listings.name: Bulldog
listings.content: Friendly hostel in the heart of the Red Light District. A coffeeshop is conveniently located on the ground floor, this is also where you get your breakfast.
listings.price: Breakfast, sheets, shower and a locker starting at €22

listings.name: Durty Nellys Inn
listings.content: Dorms are clean and the beds comfortable. The Irish pub downstairs gives discounts to people staying in the hostel (€3.5 for a pint of Amstel, €6 for a burger and chips). Breakfast 09:00-11:00. No common area apart from the bar itself.

listings.name: Flying Pig Downtown
listings.content: The "Downtown" branch, as opposed to the "Uptown" in Zuid, has more of a party vibe. Both hostels are known for their laid-back atmosphere, bars and indoor smoking areas. Free extras, check out the facility page on their website.

listings.name: Hotel Beursstraat
listings.content: Simple and clean hotel, mostly visited by (young) people who are looking for an inexpensive accommodation.

listings.name: Hotel Brian
listings.content: Very basic hotel, but breakfast and internet included.

listings.name: Hotel Tamara
listings.content: Cheap "hotel" in a great location with basic clean rooms.

listings.name: Intersail Hostel Avontuur
listings.content: A floating hostel. Small cabins, bed-length is 1.90 m, but great staff and a nice spacious sun deck. Breakfast, sheets, towels are included in the price. Shared shower and toilet. Four person cabins are better to be used for only three adults. Don't take too much luggage in these cabins.
listings.price: 4-bed private from €22.50-27.50 per bed per night. 2- and 3-bed private from 25-30 per bed per night

listings.name: Shelter City Christian Hostel
listings.content: An alcohol and drug-free Christian youth hostel right at the Red Light District. Single-sex dormitories, including breakfast, bed linen.

listings.name: St Christophers
listings.content: Part hostel, part hotel. Each room is designed by local Dutch artists.

listings.name: Stayokay Stadsdoelen
listings.content: Stayokay operates a network of 27 hostels in the Netherlands, and is the Dutch affiliate of Hostelling International. A little smaller than Stayokay Vondelpark, this location does not take groups. Free WiFi and pay internet terminals. Free security lockers are provided in the hallways outside the dorms. One of the few hostels in town who can accept under 18 year olds traveling alone (granted you have a written permission from your parents and copies of their passports). Call them for more info.

listings.name: Travel Hotel Amsterdam
listings.content: The hotel is a comfortable 2-star hotel a 5-minute walk from Amsterdam’s Central Station.

listings.name: White Tulip Hostel
listings.content: Mostly dorms, but there are also a few private rooms available. Really a basic crash-pad, but quiet and relaxed due to their 'No large groups' policy.

listings.name: Hostel Meeting Point
listings.content: Laid-back hostel. Has his own, pretty cheap, hotel bar. Smoking room (weed allowed) inside. Guests of the hostel can use free internet computers. Only dorms.

listings.name: Amsterdam Bed and Breakfast Canal View
listings.content: Has nice canal view rooms.

listings.name: Delta Hotel
listings.content: Clean rooms and friendly staff.

listings.name: Hotel Continental
listings.content: Small rooms. Shared toilets.

listings.name: Rembrandtplein Hotel
listings.content: Friendly staff, bar open all night.

listings.name: RHo Hotel
listings.content: Rooms are quiet. Parking available. Friendly staff.

listings.name: Rokin Hotel
listings.content: A 2-star renovated 17th century mansion. Very clean and good atmosphere, own parking.

listings.name: Jewel Canal Apartments
listings.content: Two canalside apartments in the center of Amsterdam, close to the Dam Square. Suitable for holiday and business stays. Free high speed internet.

listings.name: Estheréa
listings.content: A boutique hotel that consists of a row of 17th-century buildings along the Singel canal. It has 93 rooms and 2 suites. Free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Grand Hotel Amrâth Amsterdam
listings.content: An upscale hotel established in the monumental Scheepvaarthuis, the first building in Amsterdam School style that used to be the headquarters of six shipping companies. Breakfast is not included in the lower rates, but all include Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Anantara Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky
listings.content: A somewhat seedy location for a 5-star hotel, the main entrance is right on Dam Square, but the hotel backs onto the red-light district, with a view of sex-shops and peepshows.

listings.name: Park Plaza Victoria Amsterdam
listings.content: A 4-star immediately opposite Centraal Station. Free Wi-Fi in public spaces.

listings.name: Radisson Blu Hotel, Amsterdam City Center
Renaissance Amsterdam
listings.content: A 4-star hotel with conference centre, Wi-Fi access in the lobby and café.

listings.name: Sofitel Legend The Grand
listings.content: The Sofitel has views on the canals. Weather permitting, lunch is served in the courtyard.

listings.name: Natura Artis Magistra Zoo
listings.content: An entry ticket for Artis also provides admission to the Planetarium, the Aquarium and the Zoological Museum. Artis is also a botanical garden, with plants and trees gathered from all over the world, just like the animal species. Don't miss the Artis ZOOmeravonden.
listings.price: Youth (3 to 9 years) €18, adult (10 to 64 years) €21.50, seniors (65 +) €17.50

listings.name: Hortus Botanicus
listings.content: The Amsterdam Botanical Gardens — 'Hortus' as they are called by locals — used to be the Botanic Garden of the University of Amsterdam. It is one of the oldest botanical gardens in the world. Nowadays it is an independent organisation. The collection of the garden consists of more than 6,000 species. The garden regularly holds extra exhibitions and music performances.
listings.image: The Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam entrance Photo by Pejman Akbarzadeh Persian Dutch Network.jpg

listings.name: Wertheimpark
listings.content: A small park with a World War II memorial located at one of the nicest canals in Amsterdam.

listings.name: H'ART
listings.content: Founded as an outpost of the Hermitage in St Petersburg, ties were severed with the parent institution following Russia's war in Ukraine. After a hasty rebrand, the H'ART museum reopened in April 2022 with a focus on Dutch heritage in Amsterdam.
listings.price: Standard (adults and children aged 18 or over) €22.50, children up to 17 years old free

listings.name: Scheepvaartmuseum
listings.content: Het Scheepvaartmuseum reopened in late 2011 following major renovations. Stimulating, interactive exhibitions allow visitors to explore 500 years of maritime history. The building, called the Arsenal, is impressive. The Central Square, the indoor courtyard can be visited for free and takes your breath away. Also the museum shop, the restaurant and the library are open to the public free of charge.

listings.name: Verzetsmuseum
listings.content: Museum showing what Amsterdam and Holland were like during Nazi occupation. Has a very nice children's section. If you are visiting with kids and want to go to a museum about the Second World War in the Netherlands this is definitely recommended.

listings.name: De Gooyer
listings.content: It's the only windmill (1814, restored) in the centre of Amsterdam, and the closest one that's open to visitors.

listings.name: Micropia
listings.content: Museum about microbes.

listings.name: Carré Theatre
listings.content: When the theatre was founded in 1887, it was meant as a permanent circus building. It is mainly used for musicals, cabaret performances and pop concerts.

listings.name: Kriterion
listings.content: Nice small movie theatre. Also has a bar.

listings.name: Cafe Kadijk
listings.content: Cafe Kadijk is a small Indonesian restaurant that offers good food at a decent price. The restaurant has a coffee shop vibe and is located in a "trendy" area. Just outside Amsterdam's city centre, it is a bit of a walk away from the more touristy areas of the city. Patio dining and indoor dining are both available.

listings.name: De plantage
listings.content: Big restaurant with a nice terrace in the summer, open all day with breakfast, lunch and dinner.

listings.name: Restaurant Plancius
listings.content: Has a nice high tea.

listings.name: Tempura
listings.content: Nice Japanese restaurant, with a very lovely guest woman.

listings.name: De Pizzabakkers
listings.content: Hip pizza restaurant, with good stone-baked pizzas. Suitable for children. Almost always busy, so reservation is recommended.

listings.name: Aguada
listings.content: Indian and Indonesian influenced. Cosy restaurant. The rendang is a little too sweet but the thali is excellent.

listings.name: Brouwerij 't IJ
listings.content: Its label with an ostrich egg is a visual pun, as IJ and 'ei' - the word for egg - sound the same in Dutch. East of the centre, close to Artis Zoo, in a former bath house beside a windmill. A small-scale brewery where delicious beer in several varieties and strengths is brewed and sold - at a bar - on the premises. The beer is available at some specialist beer shops, and is of high quality and, in some cases, alcohol content. Internationally renowned!

listings.name: Café Smit & Voogt
listings.content: Locals love this place. It is situated inside a beautiful building and has timber booths and seating inside . There is also seating on the footpath which is well placed to catch the afternoon sun. Serves a selection of beers and other alcoholic drinks and also serves food. You can usually get a seat for a drink but better to come early or book for food. Very friendly service.

listings.name: Eden Lancaster Hotel
listings.content: A quaint 3-star hotel with 91 rooms and bags of character. Friendly and helpful English-speaking staff, quiet area and very good value for money.

listings.name: InterContinental Amstel Hotel
listings.content: Historic 5-star hotel on the banks of Amstel River, near financial, shopping and theater districts. Voted the Netherlands' best in 2008 by Condé Nast Traveller. 19th-century palace, 79 guestrooms and suites, indoor swimming pool, spa facilities including a Turkish bath.

listings.name: Hotel Allure
listings.content: Hotel Allure has rooms at Sarphiastraat and also self contained apartments at Plantage Muidergracht. The apartments are a little more expensive on a per person per night basis than the hotel and not quite as clean and tidy but may suit as they have a small kitchen (no washing machine though).

listings.name: Museum Het Schip
listings.content: A museum about the Amsterdam School architectural style, housed in a building that is probably the city's best example of that style entrance.
listings.price: EUR 15 (EUR 7.50 student) includes 20 min. guided tour

listings.name: Rembrandtpark
listings.content: Not too far west of the Vondelpark, but much quieter and larger in size.

listings.name: Westerpark
listings.content: A park at the western edge of the centre, with cultural activities in a former gas factory (Westergasfabriek). Access from Haarlemmerweg.

listings.name: De 1100 Roe (1674)
listings.content: In the Ookmeer sports fields along Ma Braunpad.

listings.name: De 1200 Roe (1632)
listings.content: Near Seineweg.

listings.name: De Bloem (1878)
listings.content: at Nieuwpoortkade.

listings.name: De Otter (1631)
listings.content: A restored and functioning sawmill, opposite Buyskade, west of the Jordaan.

listings.name: Molen van Sloten
listings.content: In Zuid, the only one open for visitors

listings.name: Dosa
listings.content: They specialise in traditional Southern Indian cuisine, especially the eponymous 'Dosa' (a rice and lentil pancake with a variety of fillings). The food is outstanding and well worth hunting out. The dosas are exceptional and a treat worthy of a visit by themselves.

listings.name: Foodhallen
listings.content: International food court with 20 food-stands housed in a large building that was once a tram depot.

listings.name: Hap Hmm
listings.content: Traditional Dutch cuisine. The restaurant may be cramped, but it does serve some quality and rustic Dutch fare. This place is cash only.

listings.name: Sora Sapporo Ramen - West
listings.content: Small ramen restaurant with friendly staff, quick service, and good selection of ramen & appetizers. Also serve beer & sake. Closes early and small seating so might want to reserve on weekends.

listings.name: TonTon Club West
listings.content: TonTon Club is an excellent place for a good night out. The place has a unique atmosphere with Japan as its inspiration. Upstairs there are arcades and button bashers, downstairs there's room for drinks and board games. You can also order Japanese snacks. Be early as tables are often reserved.

listings.name: Cafe L'Affice
listings.content: Small bar with friendly staff and a cosy and candle-lit atmosphere. Selection of beers on tap and in bottles, including a triple blonde specially made for the bar. Small selection of bar food as well.

listings.name: Club 8
listings.content: A large alternative place with lots of art on its walls. There's ping pong, a very local and fairly young crowd.

listings.name: Hotel ABBA
listings.content: Cheap but clean hotel, close to the Van Gogh and Rijksmuseum.

listings.name: MissOrtelia
listings.content: Free bikes - Wi-fi free - breakfast included.

listings.name: Holiday Inn Express Amsterdam - Sloterdijk Station
listings.content: This HIExpress is right in the midst of the web of tracks extending around Sloterdijk station, making it very convenient for travel to just about any point in Amsterdam. That said, the actual area around the hotel is a sombre office park and a huge "transferium", so it is best to only come there to sleep and have (free) breakfast.

listings.name: Meininger Hotel Amsterdam City West
listings.content: The Meininger chain's properties sit somewhere between budget hotels and hostels, with available multi-person rooms with bunk beds and on-site laundrette. The hotel is relatively new and visually attractive if rather basic inside. Again, staying in the midst of Sloterdijk is great for transit possibilities and rather unexciting regarding everything else.

listings.name: Stayokay Vondelpark
listings.content: Fairly large youth hostel, very clean and professional, operated by the Dutch affiliate of Hostelling International. Next to the pleasant Vondelpark, puts you on the south-western side of the city center and just a few blocks from the Van Gogh Museum and the Rijksmuseum. The breakfast is filling and has a social atmosphere. This location is popular with school groups. Bring a padlock for your locker, or purchase one at the desk.

listings.name: Ramada Apollo Amsterdam Centre
listings.content: The Ramada is a solid property, but calling it "Amsterdam Centre" was not even close to reality, as the hotel is at the remote end of Rembrandtpark, close to the A10 ring road running across Amsterdam-West. That said, you will find getting to the city quite easy thanks to them tram 13 stop at the hotel's back and the park provides a tranquil environment. The best rooms have great views of Amsterdam over the park; the less fortunate guests will have to enjoy residential blocks of Slotervaart. The good news is that the hotel has a top-floor restaurant, bar and terrace for everybody to enjoy the best views.

listings.name: Roemer Hotel
listings.content: Trendy boutique hotel.

listings.name: Hotel Espresso City Center
listings.content: Near Leidseplein with tram connections and bus to airport. Near Vondelpark and Museumplein. Buffet breakfast available at extra cost. Unlimited free coffee (including koffie verkeerd, the Dutch equivalent of café au lait) for guests in the lobby area.

listings.name: Amsterdam Marriott Hotel
listings.content: At the border of Oud-West and the Canal District, this old-fashioned Marriott can offer a relatively attractive rate and still has a convenient location for exploring the city centre.

listings.name: Park Plaza Amsterdam Airport
listings.content: The hotel has 19 meeting rooms as well as 6 business suites. The hotel provides free shuttle service from and to the airport as well as free wi-fi in public areas.

places.title: Artis
places.blurb: Natura Artis Magistra, commonly known just as Artis, is a zoo and botanical garden in the centre of Amsterdam.

places.title: Van Gogh Museum
places.blurb: The Van Gogh Museum is a Dutch art museum dedicated to the works of Vincent van Gogh and his contemporaries in the Museum Square in Amsterdam South, close to the Stedelijk Museum, the Rijksmuseum, and the Concertgebouw.

places.title: Royal Palace of Amsterdam

places.title: Rembrandt House Museum
places.blurb: The Rembrandt House Museum is a museum located in a former house in the Jodenbreestraat, in the center of Amsterdam.

places.title: Vondelpark
